name: Light plate carrier with pouch
description: A thin nylon carrier with a pocket front and back for an armour plate, a small flapped pouch sewn on the front and webbing on the side wings.
notes: Lying flat, front up: a coyote front panel 280 mm by 340 mm over a slightly larger back panel, shoulder straps with dark pads at the top, a black binding at the neck, a flapped pouch low on the front and a cummerbund wing either side with three webbing rows each. The two attach points are those side wings, left and right; the front carries the sewn pouch instead of webbing. The plate pockets are grids sized for a 250 mm by 320 mm front plate. Its own soft lining protects a little; the plates do the rest. CHECK VOLUME (x4.2): the reference counts the carrier packed flat. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Hardened steel front plate
description: A front armour plate cut by hand from hardened steel, its edges a little crooked, strapped onto a nylon pad.
notes: Lying strike face up: a heat-tinted steel plate 250 mm by 300 mm and 4 mm thick with uneven shooter's cuts, curved across, on an olive nylon pad, held by two black webbing straps wrapped round both with a buckle on each. It shares forged_steel_front_plate with the high steel plate; the model's finishes are this hardened one. CHECK VOLUME (x8.6) is the bounding box of a thin curved plate with straps against the steel's own volume. It is an insert, not a garment: it has no slot and is carried in a plate carrier's plate pocket, which is a grid sized for it. Its protection should count only while it sits in such a pocket; a pocket that lends its contents' protection to the wearer has no content field yet, so `protects` records the plate's own figures for when it does. No damage type for bullets exists, so pierce stands in for it. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
